facts.value: not later than the end of the first business day after discharge
facts.summary: Oregon: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the end of the first business day after discharge.
facts.evidence_quote: (1) When an employer discharges an employee or when employment is terminated by mutual agreement, all wages earned and unpaid at the time of the discharge or termination become due and payable not later than the end of the first business day after the discharge or termination.

facts.value: immediately with 48 hours notice; otherwise within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays) or the next regular payday, whichever is first
facts.summary: Oregon: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due immediately with 48 hours notice; otherwise within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays) or the next regular payday, whichever is first.
facts.evidence_quote: (2)(a) ... all wages earned and unpaid at the time of quitting become due and payable immediately if the employee has given to the employer not less than 48 hours notice ... (b) ... the wages become due and payable within five days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, after the employee has quit, or at the next regularly scheduled payday after the employee has quit, whichever event first occurs.
facts.notes: Special estimate rule applies when the employee submits time records (652.140(2)(c)).

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Oregon minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.55 standard, $16.80 Portland metro, $14.55 non-urban counties.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.55 (standard state rate); $16.80 (Portland Metro Area); $14.55 (Non-Urban counties) Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Premium pay required after 10 hours a day in nonfarm canneries, driers, or packing plants and in mills, factories or manufacturing establishments (excluding sawmills, planning mills, shingle mills, and logging camps). The Oregon minimum wage is adjusted annually on July 1 based on a set formula. There is a higher minimum wage in the Portland metro area and a lower minimum wage in non-urban counties. facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page. Regional rates: value_numeric left empty so no single figure acts as a statewide default.

facts.value: Yes. The independent contractor information must be reported not later than 20 days after the date the employer engages or reengages an individual who is an independent contractor for more than 20 days.

facts.evidence_quote: Independent Contractor Reporting Required?: Yes. The independent contractor information must be reported not later than 20 days after the date the employer engages or reengages an individual who is an independent contractor for more than 20 days.
